title: Mastering CSS View Transitions
summary: Learn how to create complex UI animations like card-to-page morphs, list reordering, and circular theme wipes using the CSS View Transitions API. This lesson demonstrates how a single CSS property can replace heavy animation libraries for both single-page and multi-page applications.

transcript.text: A card becomes a page. One line of CSS, no animation library.
Give the card image and the page header the same view-transition-name. The browser snapshots both states and morphs one into the other.
In a single page app, one startViewTransition call wraps the DOM update.
Reorder a list? Give every item its own unique name. Sort, filter, delete. Each row slides to its new spot for free.
Two items with the same name, and the whole transition is skipped.
Theme toggle. The whole page is one snapshot called root. Animate a clip-path circle on view-transition-new of root.
Dark mode spreads out from the button you clicked.
A modal that grows from its button. The button holds the name. On open, the name moves to the dialog.
It expands out of the place you tapped instead of fading in from nowhere.
It works across real page loads too. One @rule, navigation: auto on both pages.
Multi-page site, no framework, same morph. Chrome and Safari ship it today.
Without support, you get an instant swap. Nothing breaks.
Four morphs. One property. Think like a senior UX designer.

on_screen_text: A modal born from its button.
before_after: Demonstrates the transition from static UI updates (instant swaps) to smooth, browser-native morphing animations for cards, lists, themes, and modals.
